classification.difficultyReason: Compare two graphs of the same data and notice that one axis silently skips 400. This needs careful scale reading, then a justification.

content.prompt: The two graphs show the number of visitors to a museum each month. Which graph is not misleading, and why?

answer.short: Graph B. In Graph A the vertical scale is irregular: 300 to 500 takes the same space as 100 to 200.
answer.worked: Both graphs start at 0, so look at the vertical scales. Graph A labels $0,100,200,300,500,600$ at equal spacing, so the jump from 300 to 500 looks the same as each rise of 100. This makes the April increase of 200 look smaller than it is. Graph B has a regular scale in steps of 100, so it shows the data fairly.
